articles.title: Wardogs Surpasses 1 Million Copies Sold on Day One, Blows Past 300k Peak Concurrent Players on Steam
articles.summary: Wardogs has already surpassed a million copies sold and is lighting up Steam's concurrent player charts. Earlier today, developer Bulkhead launched its brand new all-out warfare FPS, Wardogs.
body: “To cross a million copies sold as we launch into early access is mental,” said Joe Brammer, CEO at Bulkhead. “We've spent the last few months showing people exactly what Wardogs is, what it isn't, and at one point literally gave everyone ten reasons not to buy it. We didn't want people buying into blind hype. So seeing more than one million people choose to jump in and play the game at early access launch means a huge amount to all of us. But this is still early access. We've got things to fix, things we want to improve and a lot more we want to build. The best thing players can do now is keep playing, keep telling us what they think and keep giving us those ridiculous Wardogs moments.”

Wardogs is currently only available on PC, making its debut sales numbers all the more impressive, but it is coming to consoles. Bulkhead confirmed that Wardogs is targeting a 2028 release for PS5 and Xbox, but didn't offer a concrete release date. The developer has also noted that it expects the hype to die down eventually, as they plan to take their time when it comes to releasing new content and therefore there may be drops in player counts.

articles.title: Dead or Alive 6 Last Round Project Manager Sparks Debate After Revealing Koei Tecmo is Dialing Back the Game's 'Sexy Costumes'
articles.summary: Dead or Alive 6 Last Round Project Manager Tsuyoshi Iuchi has sparked a debate within the fighting game community after explaining why the team at Koei Tecmo is dialing back on making sexy costumes.
body: Dead or Alive is a fighting game franchise with a fiercely loyal fanbase and a dedicated competitive scene. Despite these factors, it’s also known as the fighting game series with the most fanservice — a label that’s hard to get away from, given the jiggle physics, dating-sim-heavy spinoff games, and sexy outfits that exist in abundance in almost every DoA title.

While Dead or Alive 7 is in active development, DoA 6 Last Round is still getting content, including a new character that was just announced yesterday. Minato’s addition to the roster hasn’t come without controversy; some fans are accusing the schoolgirl of being a copy/paste of Honoka, while others are pointing toward a September 9 Famitsu interview that included some divisive remarks from the game’s development team.

Of these remarks, one is standing out from the rest: Project Manager Tsuyoshi Iuchi confirmed that Koei Tecmo is making the decision to step back from making more sexy outfits for Dead or Alive’s characters. This is a big change for the franchise, and one that’s been met with backlash and confusion from its fanbase.

articles.title: Wardogs Has A Massive Start On Steam, But Players Face Brutal Server Queues
articles.summary: A big new military FPS, Wardogs (not to be confused with the 2016 Jonah Hill/Miles Teller crime-comedy War Dogs) launched today in early access on Steam, and it's off to a hot start.
body: Given the flood of players, developer Bulkhead instituted a server queue system, and this quickly became something of a meme on social media. Players shared screenshots of the queue and their place in it--some people reported having more than 300,000 people in line in front of them. Yeesh.

Bulkhead responded to the brutal queueing situation, saying it was partly due to the developer being "rate limited." The company said it was working with Valve to resolve this limit and get an increase in line with "larger titles."
Things got worse, temporarily albeit, for some, as Bulkhead made the decision to kick everyone from the queue as a fix that, in theory, would help more players get into the game faster.

Bulkhead boss Joe Brammer gave an update on the queuing situation, saying the queue itself is not "specifically broken," but instead he said Wardogs didn't get the kind of treatment that AAA games receive when it comes to rate limits.

articles.title: T-Mobile Is Already Teasing Its Apple iPhone 18 "On Us" Promotion Ahead of the Official Preorder Launch
articles.summary: Apple's newest lineup of iPhone 18 phones, which includes the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the all new iPhone 18 Duo, was announced during Apple's "Surprise and Shine" Event on September 9.
body: The Experience Beyond plan costs $100 per month for a single line with AutoPay (plus taxes and fees). The plan gives you unlimited talk, text, and 5G premium data. Other perks include Netflix (Standard with ads) and Hulu subscriptions, Apple TV for $3/mo, unlimited mobile hotspot, T-Satellite, phone upgrade eligibility every year, and a 5 year price guarantee. International travelers can also benefit from unlimited text and 30GB of high-speed data in Canada and Mexico and unlimited text and 15GB of high-speed data in over 215 other countries.

Currently the only promotion listed is for the iPhone 18 Pro. There's a good chance, however, that we'll see similar discounts for the iPhone 18 Pro Max and the iPhone Duo. The iPhone Duo would be an especially attractive offer, since the phone will carry a sticker price of $1,999. Usually with these types of promotions you end up paying more for the phone compared to buying it outright, but who wants to spend that much money right out of the gate for a phone? If you intend to stick with T-Mobile's 5G network anyways, then that's all the more reason to start using Apple's newest iPhone immediately.

articles.title: The iPhone Duo Might Be One of the First Foldables That's Good For Gaming
articles.summary: I've been hooked on foldables for years now, and I carry the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra on me every day. And while that phone is incredible for most of what I need to do on a day-to-day basis, gaming has never felt amazing on it.
body: A big part of that comes down to the aspect ratio of the larger inner screen. While there are a lot of games that will adopt the 4:3 aspect ratio, there are plenty that just don't, leading to either an ugly, stretched picture or giant black bars. In Hearthstone, for example, I have the choice of having a third of the screen blocked off, or have it stretch out to fill the screen, only to cut off a good portion of what's supposed to be displayed.

There have been several times where I've tried to fullscreen that game, only to not be able to read a card on one of the far edges of the battlefield, because the image is cut off. Now, a lot of this does come down to the developers. Certainly, Blizzard has the resources to update Hearthstone to accommodate the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra's square display. But, I've been testing these foldables for the last seven years and things haven't improved. If Blizzard hasn't done anything by now, I doubt it's going to any time soon. I'd rather not leave it up to individual developers here.
points: I've been hooked on foldables for years now, and I carry the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra on me every day.
And while that phone is incredible for most of what I need to do on a day-to-day basis, gaming has never felt amazing on it.

articles.title: Amazon Prime Members Get Doom Eternal And 10 More Games For Free In September
articles.summary: The next wave of monthly games for Amazon Luna has been revealed, and if you're a fan of first-person shooters, then you're in for a treat. The headline act is Doom Eternal, or if you'd prefer your guns to be chatterboxes, you can also grab the delightfully weird High on Life.
body: Several new GameNight titles will also be available throughout the month, so if you're in the mood for some social gaming, you can check out kaiju-powered board game fun in King of Tokyo, test your general knowledge in Quiz Time: Guinness World Records, aim for a strike in Bowling Mayhem, and explore Cranium Planet.

As part of its September update, Amazon Luna is also introducing a Remote Play feature. This will allow people to play games together--even if they aren’t in the same room--and it should work nicely with the multiplayer titles featured in the Luna streaming library.

As mentioned above, you can download some pretty good action games, and if you want to experience the formative years of Doom, you can also check out the first two games in the franchise. Botany Manor is also recommended as it offers both a chance to flex your brain muscles and your green thumb. Rims Racing is a rock-solid motorbike simulator, and Just Die Already is an "old people mayhem sandbox game" from the team behind the Goat Simulator series. Several of these games are already available to claim, and the rest will roll out in weekly waves.

articles.title: Peacock's Friday the 13th Prequel Promises ‘More Than You Think’ From Jason, Showrunner Says
articles.summary: October's biggest horror TV show stars Linda Cardellini as Pam Voorhees, Jason's mom from the 1980 F13 movie. It has a brain.
body: In my opinion, Brad Caleb Kane has the hardest job on television this fall: turning Friday the 13th, a franchise built for decades on Jason Voorhees violent rampages, into a sustainable series for A24 and Peacock. When I point out that it feels like a near-impossible challenge, he does not miss a beat.
“ I'm here for it. I'm not afraid. Going in with a full heart, man. I'm happy to do it.”

Crystal Lake finds Pam Voorhees (Linda Cardellini), about a decade before the events of the original Friday the 13th, wrecked by the drowning death of her young son, Jason. But there’s more to Pam’s present — and past — than any fan of the series might guess. Kane’s version of Crystal Lake is a little corner of America sinking into a paranoid, deeply unsettled era where every twist is compounded by Pam’s grief over Jason.
Sound heavy? Don’t worry: The kills are sick. And there are lots of them.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7's Future in Fortnite Is Unclear, but There’s Hope
articles.summary: Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy director Naoki Hamaguchi spoke about Square Enix's relationship with Fortnite in a recent interview. Although he didn't directly answer whether Final Fantasy characters would eventually be part of Fortnite 's extensive roster of skins, some hope lingers among fans.
body: Fortnite 's latest season, Chapter 7 Season 4, has two main themes: video games and hacking. Combining the two made it possible for Epic Games to bring an array of new video game IPs to its Battle Royale. This season, players can snag cosmetics inspired by Sonic the Hedgehog, Crash Bandicoot, Mega Man, and Spyro. There are many more to come, with confirmed upcoming appearances from Kingdom Hearts ' Sora and Persona 5 's Joker.

"What I can say right now is that, looking back at the history of Final Fantasy 7, fans might notice this, but we haven’t had a lot of very major collaborations with other IPs. This is mostly because we wanted to be selective to protect the brand of Final Fantasy 7. But what I can say now is that we are, you know, considering a lot of, you know, different collaborations at the moment. So, you know, whether Fortnite is included in the list of potential collaboration partners, that’s something for the fans to look forward to."
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

articles.title: Metroid Dread studio MercurySteam appears to confirm it's making Metroid Ravenous, addressing a lingering question from yesterday's Nintendo Direct
articles.summary: Spanish studio MercurySteam - the developer of Metroid Dread - seems to be the studio behind yesterday's Nintendo Direct showcase stopper, Metroid Ravenous.
body: Questions were raised after the Direct showcase because, despite the obvious visual similarities between Metroid Dread and Ravenous, MercurySteam's name did not appear in the Ravenous trailer or on any associated press gumpf. MercurySteam's social accounts were also quiet following the event.

I sought clarification from Nintendo and from MercurySteam this morning because of this, but heard nothing back - though this silence is not unusual for Nintendo, which often doesn't disclose developers until close to a game's release.

Nonetheless, MercurySteam appears to have ended speculation today by retweeting yesterday's Metroid Ravenous trailer with a ninja emoji and a heart emoji, presumably signalling some kind of stealth development situation. The same trailer was shared on LinkedIn by the company moments ago as well.

Metroid Ravenous seems to closely follow the Metroid Dread template, offering a side-on Metroid adventure, albeit one that plays with perspective a lot. Ravenous appears more colourful and less oppressive than Dread, and its montage of energetic gameplay lit-up Nintendo's Direct yesterday afternoon.

articles.title: Survival Horror Movie Whalefall Unveils Its Most Chilling Trailer Yet
articles.summary: I don't know about you, but I've never wondered what it would feel like to be swallowed up by a whale while taking a morning swim. Fortunately for all of us, Pulitzer Prize-winning author Daniel Kraus has chosen to answer that question with his novel Whalefall, and its movie adaptation is out next…
body: Whalefall follows diver Jay Gardiner (Austin Abrams), who ends up getting swallowed by a giant sperm whale. With only an hour of oxygen left, he has to find a way out before he suffocates and becomes whale food. The new trailer is narrated by his father (Josh Brolin), who provides nuggets of wisdom like, "Remember: survivors survive." Thanks, pops!

Whalefall stars Austin Abrams, who's about to have a terrifying autumn. While you and I might be going apple picking or strolling through a pumpkin patch, he'll fight his way out of a whale after trying to survive a zombie apocalypse in next week's Resident Evil.

Abrams won't be playing series favorite Leon S. Kennedy, but instead a new character created for the film. "I'd rather watch a movie starring a schlub who's, like, out of shape and has never fired a gun before!" Resident Evil director Zach Cregger recently told Polygon. Abrams isn't an out-of-shape schlub, but he's definitely the guy who can nail the feeling of being a scared player on the run from a hungry zombie. And, in Whalefall, a hungry sperm whale.

articles.title: Nintendo of America thanks fans for dealing with tariff-related price hikes by encouraging them to spend more money in a new sale
articles.summary: Nintendo of America is currently facing a class action lawsuit for refusing to pass tariff refunds onto customers, and it's against that backdrop it today announced a "Customer Appreciation Sale" apparently made possible by those rebates.
body: In a blog post, Nintendo called this one of its "largest promotions ever", and included the following line which has had people scratching their heads: "While Nintendo absorbed most tariff-related costs, the refunds helped make promotions like this one possible."

A quick recap: following the introduction of tariffs by the current US government last year, Nintendo increased the price of multiple products in the country, citing "market conditions" as justification.

Nintendo, in this sale announcement, argues that it "absorbed" most of the costs, but the company has received a refund. The US consumers who bought Nintendo products since the price increase also suffered increased costs thanks to the tariffs, but they aren't receiving refunds. The reason this is rubbing people the wrong way is because Nintendo is thanking them for dealing with increased costs by encouraging them to spend more money.

The counter argument is, hey, why look a gift horse in the mouth? This is a discount on some games and peripherals at a time when buying new stuff in this market is awfully expensive. This ultimately could be seen as a gesture of goodwill, and one Switch owners could benefit from.

articles.title: "What in the vibe-coded s*** is this" - RuneScape players revolt as gen-AI copycat game appears and eventually attracts the eye of Jagex
articles.summary: A clone of Old School RuneScape that appeared on the internet this week, and stoked the ire of the RuneScape community, has quickly been shut down.
body: The clone was made by e OpenAI employee Rohan Varma, who used the GPT-6 Astra to build a version of RuneScape he named Elderwood, which was playable in a browser.

In a video - itself created with gen-AI - uploaded to X, we see a character created and spawning outside Lumbridge castle, with an inventory of bread, coins, and basic tools. We then see the same character fighting giant rats, chopping trees, and equipping steel armour. It looks incredibly similar to Old School RuneScape save for a few inconsistencies..

But as Verma continued to experiment and share their progress on X, the posts caught the attention of the Old School RuneScape community who were displeased with what they found. In a thread posted to the 2007scape Reddit, users were not shy in their criticisms.

"What in the vibe coded shit is this. They even straight up ripped art assets shameless," wrote user RangeCreed. "Love the tweet format. AI bros can only speak in numbers and bullet lists (ideally both at once)," adds Lekamil, while X user Toppo simply summarised the situation with the following: "tl;dr garbage."
points: A clone of Old School RuneScape that appeared on the internet this week, and stoked the ire of the RuneScape community, has quickly been shut down.
The clone was made by e OpenAI employee Rohan Varma, who used the GPT-6 Astra to build a version of RuneScape he named Elderwood, which was playable in a browser.

body: In the series, three strangers survive the opening days of the Republic of Sotoa's invasion of the Federation of Central Usea. Josh Holloway stars as a pilot with nowhere to land, Brandon Routh as a doctor who saved his enemy, and Tamlyn Tomita as a news anchor silenced for telling the truth.
HOUR ZERO will span four total episodes and will be available on IGN.com and IGN's YouTube Channel.

videos.title: Marvel's Wolverine Review
videos.summary: Marvel's Wolverine reviewed on PS5 Pro by Simon Cardy.
body: Marvel’s Wolverine certainly doesn’t skimp when it comes to violence, and gives you plenty of opportunities to enact it with style. But it takes more than blood to get my heart pumping, and it’s in Logan’s surprisingly nuanced tale of self-acceptance that I felt most connected to this latest portrayal of the most famous of the X-Men. That story is tasked with doing most of the heavy lifting here, with the initially slick and satisfying combat wearing thin well before its conclusion, but even that solid character work can’t quite carry the weight it needs to. Marvel’s Wolverine, much like its lead, is built on a firm skeleton, but what’s crafted around it isn’t nearly as strong.
points: Marvel's Wolverine reviewed on PS5 Pro by Simon Cardy.
